1. [P1] Cache creation tokens can still be double-counted.

Both the non-streaming Responses conversion and streaming output paths only subtract cached_tokens, while separately reporting cache_creation_input_tokens.

If the upstream total input token count already includes cache creation tokens, clients will still overcount usage when summing these fields.

For example, given a total input of 100 tokens, 30 cache-read tokens, and 20 cache-write tokens, the current output reports a combined total of 120 tokens.

Recommendation: Clarify the semantics of the upstream total input token field, and add a test where cache-read and cache-write tokens are both non-zero simultaneously.

This is the same issue identified in the first finding of PR #1615.

2. [P2] Invalid cache token counts can still alter billing.

The helper returns 0 when cached > prompt. However, both the Chat writer and Responses writer subsequently reconstruct the internal input token count as 0 + cached.

For example, if the upstream reports prompt=100, cached=150, the resulting billable input token count becomes 150.

Recommendation: Preserve the original upstream total input token count directly for internal Usage() accounting, rather than reconstructing it from the clamped values.

This PR has merge conflicts with the target branch. Could you please resolve the conflicts and update the PR ?

Thanks!

Thanks for the review. Both findings are already handled on main by #1615 (merged after this PR was opened): `uncachedInputTokens` now subtracts cache reads and cache writes (Responses `cached_creation_tokens`), so 100 total / 30 read / 20 write reports `input_tokens: 50` (`TestE2E_ToResponses_Stream_InputTokensExcludeCacheReadsAndWrites`), and internal accounting keeps the upstream total instead of rebuilding it from the clamped value (`..._Billing_KeepsUpstreamTotalWhenCacheExceedsPrompt`, chat and Responses). Merging main into this branch leaves nothing of #1620 that main does not already do, so it is superseded by #1615 and can be closed.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
Both findings are already handled on main by https://github.com/OpenCSGs/csghub-server/pull/1615
